translations.text: Dearest people, your faith will be the stronger if you hear about God's saints and how they earned the heavenly kingdom;
and you can call on them more familiarly if the way they lived becomes known to you through the preaching of teachers.
This holy man Clement, whom we honour on this present feast day, was the disciple of the blessed apostle Peter.
He grew so greatly in spiritual learning and diligence that the apostle Peter chose him to be pope of the Roman people after his own day,
and before his passion ordained him pope and set him on his episcopal seat, so that he would have charge of the Christian people.
He had ordained two bishops before that, Linus and Cletus, but he did not set them on his seat as he did this holy man whom we honour today.
So then, after Peter's passion, Clement flourished in the beauty of good virtues, so that he was pleasing to Jews, heathens and Christians alike.
He pleased the heathen people, because he did not insult their gods with scorn, but showed them with learned reasoning what they were,
[?] and where those whom they worshipped as gods were born, and he made known their way of life and their end with clear proofs;
and he said that they themselves could easily come to God's mercy if they turned entirely away from their erroneous worship.
He won the favour of the Jewish people because he truly affirmed that their forefathers were called God's friends, and that God gave them a holy law to guide their lives;
and he said that they would be foremost among God's chosen if they obeyed his commandments with faith.
By the Christians he was loved most, because he kept every district in mind by name, and did not allow the poor Christians of those districts to be reduced to open beggary,
but with daily preaching he urged the rich and the wealthy to relieve the poverty of the Christians with their wealth, so that they would not be defiled by gifts from heathen men.
And Dionysius, God's witness, who through the teaching and miracles of Paul the Apostle had turned to Christ's faith with a holy way of life, went at that time from Greece to the holy pope Clement,
[?] Peter's successor, and he received him with great honour, and out of reverence for his holy life admitted him into his close friendship and kept him with love.

Then after a time the blessed Clement said to the holy man Dionysius, "Let power be given to you to bind and to loose, as it is to me; and go to the kingdom of the Franks, and preach the gospel to them and the glory of the kingdom of heaven."
Dionysius then obeyed his commands and went with companions to the land of the Franks, preaching Christianity with great miracles, so much so that the fierce heathens, as soon as they saw him,
either fell down at his feet, obeying him and God, or, if any of them resisted, that one was seized with such great terror that he fled from his presence at once.

Then the whole kingdom of the Franks was turned to God's faith through the preaching and miracles of the blessed man Dionysius; and he also sent some of his companions to Spain, so that they might make known the word of life to that people.
So then, Clement the Roman pope was accused before the emperor Trajan because of the great spread of Christianity that he had brought about everywhere in his realm.

Then the emperor Trajan sent back letters saying that the holy pope Clement must bow to idol-worship, or else be sent over the sea into exile to a certain wilderness, where Christians condemned for their faith lived in exile.
The emperor's command was then carried out, and Almighty God granted Clement such great grace that the heathen judge lamented his journey with weeping,
saying, "May the God whom you worship comfort you and help you in your exile."
And then he ordered him to be taken to a ship, and provided all the things he needed to live on. Then the ship was filled with Christian men who would not leave the holy pope.
When he came to the wilderness, he found more than two thousand Christian men there, who had been sentenced to long punishment in the marble quarry,
and who greatly rejoiced at his coming, saying with one voice, "Behold, here is our shepherd; behold, here is the comforter of our toil and labour."
When he had strengthened and comforted their weary minds with encouraging words, he learned that every day they fetched water for themselves on their shoulders from over six miles away.
Then the blessed bishop said, "Let us pray with firm faith to the Lord Saviour that he open the veins of his spring nearer at hand for us, his confessors, so that we may rejoice in his benefits."

When this prayer was finished, the bishop looked on every side, and then saw a white lamb standing on the right side. It beckoned with its right foot, as if it wanted to show where the vein of water was.
Then Clement understood the lamb's sign, and said, "Open the earth in this place, where the lamb pointed."
His companions then carried out his command, and immediately at the first digging an immense spring burst out, and it ran forth in a great stream.
Lo, they all rejoiced greatly then, and thanked God for the relief of their toil.
Then the saying was fulfilled that they had spoken at the bishop's coming: "Behold, here is our shepherd; behold, here is the comforter of our toil."
This miracle then spread through the neighbouring districts, and they all came to visit the holy bishop with reverence, praying that he would strengthen them with his teaching.
He then turned them all to faith in God, and within a few days he baptized five hundred people there; and many churches were then built everywhere, and idols were thrown down;
so that within the space of one year no heathen temple was to be found anywhere within a hundred miles.

Then it happened that some of the heathens were provoked by envy, and sent a message to the emperor, telling him that his people were all stirred up together and wholly turned away from his worship by Clement, the bishop of the Christians.

Then the heathen emperor Trajan was greatly stirred up, and sent a cruel general named Aufidianus, who had killed many Christians with various tortures, to destroy the holy bishop together with the faithful people.
Then the wicked executioner Aufidianus, when he could not frighten the Christians with any threat,
because they were all hurrying to martyrdom together, rejoicing, let the people go, and tried to force the bishop alone to worship the idols;
but when he saw that he could in no way bend him, he said to his subordinates, "Take him to the middle of the sea, tie an anchor to his neck, and push him out into the midst of the deep."
It was then done at the command of the cruel executioner, and a great multitude of the Christians stood on the seashore,
weeping and praying to the Almighty, who created sea and earth, that they might attend to his holy body with their services.
Then his two disciples, Phoebus and Cornelius, said, "O brothers, let us pray to our Lord with one mind, that he reveal to us the venerable presence of his holy martyr."
Lo, then the sea, by God's command, flowed back and opened for them a dry passage three miles long, so that the Christians boldly went in,
and they found a new coffin of marble, shaped like a church, and the body of the holy martyr laid inside it through the ministry of angels, and the anchor lying beside him.

Then it was revealed to them that he had obtained from God that each year, around the time of his martyrdom, the sea would provide dry ground for the people for seven days, so that within that time they might visit his holy body.
That is to the praise and glory of our Saviour, who prepared that venerable tomb for his holy martyr.
Then through this sign all the unbelievers became Christian, so that there was no one at all to be found in that land, either heathen or Jewish, who was not converted to the Christian faith.
Truly, at that holy coffin heavenly healings are granted to sick bodies through the intercession of the holy martyr.
Whoever visits his tomb sick at his feast-time goes back rejoicing and healthy.

There the blind are given light, and those possessed by devils are restored to their senses, and all kinds of afflicted people are gladdened there; and all the faithful enjoy his benefits, and the mysteries of God are fulfilled there with honour.
It happened then in a certain year at his feast-time that a woman with her newborn child visited the holy man among other people.

Then, when the days of the festival had ended, the sea came suddenly roaring, and the people hurried away in great haste, and the woman, because of the sudden commotion, did not take care of her child before she reached land.
She then spent the twelve months in sorrow, and again at the turning of the year, at the same feast-time, she ran ahead of the people and approached the tomb weeping, praying thus,
"You, Lord Saviour, who raised the widow's only son to life, look on me with mercy, so that I, through the intercession of your saint who rests here, may be granted what I earnestly ask."
Then with this prayer she looked toward the place where she had earlier left the child, and found it sleeping just as she had laid it down before.
Then with great joy she woke it, and kissed it, weeping. Then between the kisses she asked the child how it had fared during the whole time of the year's course.
The child answered its mother, "My mother, I did not know how this year's course came to an end, because I rested in soft sleep, just as you left me, until you now woke me again."
The faithful people then, rejoicing greatly, praised and blessed the Almighty Saviour, who honours his saints with signs and wonders, and so makes their merits manifest.
Often people of little faith ponder with their foolish reasoning why Almighty God would ever allow the heathens to be able to kill his saints with all kinds of torments;
but we will now relate to you some demonstrations from the old law, and also from the new,
how mightily the ruling Lord often rescued his saints from heathen armies or cruel persecutors, and shamefully put their adversaries to confusion.
It happened in the fourteenth year of the reign of Hezekiah, king of the Jews, that Sennacherib, king of Syria, brought many peoples under his rule with great power,
and wished to do the same to the believing king Hezekiah, and sent his general Rabshakeh to the city of Jerusalem with a great host, and with letters he scorned the might of Almighty God,
speaking thus to the besieged people: "Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with false hope that God will rescue you from me.
I have subdued and conquered many nations, and their gods could not shield them against my might. What god is there who can defend this city against my army?"
Well then, King Hezekiah threw off his purple robe and put haircloth on his body, and carried the letters into God's temple, and with outstretched limbs prayed, saying thus,
"Lord, God of hosts, you who sit above the host of angels, you alone are God of all nations; you made the heavens, and the earth, and all creatures.
Incline your ear and hear, open your eyes and see these words which Sennacherib has sent in mockery and reproach of you and your people.
Truly he overthrew the heathen gods and burned them, because they were not gods but the handiwork of men, made of wood and of stone, and therefore he smashed them.
Deliver us now, Lord, from his threats and his might, so that all nations may know that you alone are Almighty God."
Hezekiah also sent his counsellors, clothed in haircloth, to the prophet Isaiah, saying thus, "Lift up your prayers for the people of Israel,
so that Almighty God may hear the words which the king of Syria sent in scorn and reproach of his great majesty."

Then the prophet Isaiah answered the messengers, "Tell your lord that he should be unafraid. God Almighty says: Sennacherib shall not shoot an arrow into the city of Jerusalem, nor overpower it with his shield;
but I will put a ring in his nose and a bridle in his lips, and I will lead him back to his people, and I will cause him to fall by the edge of the sword in his own homeland;

and I will shield the city for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David." Then in that night God's angel went out and slew of the Syrian king's army one hundred thousand men and eighty-five thousand.
Next morning Sennacherib arose and saw the dead bodies, and returned in great shame to the city of Nineveh.
It then happened that while he was praying to his idol, his two sons killed him with a sword, just as the prophet had prophesied through the Spirit of God.

Again afterwards Nebuchadnezzar, the Chaldean king, ordered the three believing young men, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, to be bound hand and foot and thrown into a burning furnace, because they would not pray to his idol.
But Almighty God, in whom they steadfastly believed, sent his angel into the furnace with the young men, and he then shook the flame out of the furnace,
so that the fire could not harm them, but it shot out of the furnace forty-nine fathoms and burned up the executioners who had kindled the fire.
Then the king examined the hair and bodies of the three young men, saying thus: "Blessed be your God, who sent his angel and so mightily delivered his servants from the burning furnace."
Also afterwards, in the days of King Cyrus, the Babylonians accused the prophet Daniel, because he had overthrown their idol,
and said with one mind to the aforesaid King Cyrus, "Hand Daniel over to us, who overthrew our god Bel and killed the dragon in which we believed.
If you protect him, we will destroy you and your household." Then the king saw that they were of one mind, and under compulsion handed the prophet over to them.

They then threw him into a pit in which there were seven lions, to which two oxen and two sheep were given daily; but every food was then withheld from them for six days, so that they would devour the man of God.
At that time there was another prophet in the land of Judea, whose name was Habakkuk, who was carrying food to his reapers in the field.
Then God's angel came to him and said, "Habakkuk, carry the food to Babylon and give it to Daniel, who sits in the lions' pit."
Habakkuk answered the angel, "Oh, sir, I have never seen the city, nor do I know the pit."
Then the angel seized him by the hair and carried him to Babylon, and set him above the pit.
Then Habakkuk called out, "You servant of God, Daniel, take this gift which God has sent you."
Daniel said, "My Lord Saviour, praise and honour be to you that you have remembered me." And he then partook of the food.
Truly God's angel straightway, with swift flight, brought the server of the dish, Habakkuk, back to where he had taken him from before.
Then King Cyrus, on the seventh day, went sorrowfully to the lions' pit and looked in, and behold, Daniel was sitting unharmed in the midst of the lions.

Then the king cried out with a loud voice, "Great is the God in whom Daniel believes." And with that word he drew him out of the den, and ordered those who had earlier wanted to destroy him to be thrown in.
The king's command was quickly carried out, and the prophet's persecutors were thrust in among the lions, and they straightway tore them all apart with greedy jaws.
Then the king said, "Let all who dwell on earth fear and dread the God of Daniel, for he is the Redeemer and Saviour, working signs and wonders in heaven and on earth."
In the New Testament, after Christ's passion, and his resurrection and ascension into heaven, the Jews were filled with envy against his apostles, and put them in prison.
On that same night God's angel undid the locks of the prison and led them out, saying, "Go to the temple, and preach to the people the word of life."
And they did so. Then in the morning the Jews deliberated about the destruction of the apostles, and sent to the prison to have them fetched.
Then the officers opened the prison, and found no one.
They then told their elders, "We found the prison firmly shut, and the guards standing outside, but we found no one inside."
Again afterwards Herod, king of Judea, put the apostle Peter in prison, bound with two chains, and set guards inside and outside:

but on the night before the wicked king meant to kill him in the morning, God's angel came shining from heaven and led him out through the iron gates; and in the morning the prison still stood firmly locked.
Domitian, the heathen emperor, ordered the evangelist John to be thrown into boiling oil, but he, through God's protection, came out as unharmed as he had been when he was thrown in.
A certain idolater gave this same John poison to drink, but after that drink he remained sound and unharmed.
Paul the apostle wrote about himself, and said that he spent a day and a night in the depth of the sea.
Again, on a certain occasion a viper seized him by the finger, but he shook it off into a burning fire, and he felt nothing at all of the poison.
No earthly man can make known in writing, nor recount with tongue, how often the Almighty Ruler has rescued his chosen ones from various perils, to the praise and honour of his majesty.

But he very often permits the wicked to afflict his saints severely, sometimes with grievous persecution, sometimes with slaying, so that the cruel persecution may turn out to be eternal rest for the righteous, and eternal punishment for the killers.
The psalmist said, "Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the Lord delivers them from all of these."
God delivers his chosen ones in two ways, openly and secretly. They are delivered openly when they are rescued in the sight of men, just as we have now told you.
They are delivered in a hidden way when they come through martyrdom to heavenly honours. If they suffer for the true faith or for righteousness, they are then martyrs.
If, however, they are killed while innocent, their innocence leads them to the fellowship of God's saints, for innocence always remains free from care.
But if anyone suffers persecution for his sins, and acknowledges himself, so that he earnestly prays for God's mercy, then the temporary punishment forestalls the eternal condemnation.
The two thieves who hung with Christ were punished for their evil deeds, but one of them prayed to Christ with great faith, saying, "Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
Christ answered him, "Truly I tell you, this very day you will be with me in the joy of paradise."
We may lose transitory goods against our will, but we never lose the eternal goods against our will.
Though the cruel robber may rob us of our possessions, or deprive us of life, he cannot take away from us our faith or eternal life, unless we destroy ourselves of our own will.
May the true Lord rescue us from all perils and lead us to the eternal life, he who lives and reigns forever without end. Amen.
